title: Two-ink woods

reference.source: Reference 16: two-color print with a black key, 1200 × 1500 px
reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: A mint plate of lobed foliage grained like a riso screen, a flat pink plate, and a 4 px black key drawn over them 2 px out of register, with Mindgut's robot standing in the glade.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 1200 × 1500 and every length scales with the canvas

masses.does: Lobed blobs around the oval of the glade.

size.does: Radius of the foliage blobs, 70 to 160 px at 1.

wobble.does: Noise on each blob's rim, the hand in the drawn edge.

trunk.does: Width of the tree, 76 px at 1. 0 removes it.

mushrooms.does: Caps in the cluster at the lower left, each with its gills.

disc.does: Radius of the pink disc, 92 px at 1.

dots.does: Rings with a center dot drifting near the disc.

robot.does: Height of Mindgut's robot, 250 px at 1. 0 removes it.

key.does: Width of the black line. Measured 4 px, hatch strokes 3.6 px.

hatch.does: Count of short curved strokes inside the foliage, denser where the shade field is dark.

bark.does: Spacing of the wavy lines along the trunk.

grainG.does: Speckle of the mint plate. Measured σ 14 on a 127, 197, 165 ink.

grainP.does: Speckle of the pink plate. Measured σ 5.

rough.does: How much the grain breaks the edges of every plate and the key.

misreg.does: Offset of the color plates from the key, as the drum feeds each pass.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: Mint plate up close: σ 14 speckle, 2 px specks, no gradient

techniques.name: Pull
techniques.implementation: Bark: wavy lines on a 9 px pitch along the trunk

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: Flying dots: rings with a center dot

pass_order: shape fields at 1/3 resolution: lobed blobs around the glade's oval, four ground masses, the trunk as a tapered band; Catmull-Rom up to full size
pink plate on a full-res canvas: disc, three blobs, the robot's body

key plate on a full-res canvas: hatch strokes inside the foliage where the shade field is dark, bark lines along the trunk, mushroom caps and gills, rings with dots, the robot's outline, eyes and grille

per pixel: ground; the mint plate shifted 2 px with its edge wobbled by the grain and its tone speckled; the pink plate shifted the other way; the key as the field's zero band plus the drawn strokes, its edge broken by the same grain

measured.kmeans6: ground .513, light mint .136, key .116, mint .115, pink .064, dark mint .056
measured.misregistration_px: about 2, read by eye on the foliage edges
measured.rejected: a smooth gradient inside the foliage: the mint plate is flat with speckle, its only shading is the hatching

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Mint and salmon palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: The glade is generated; patches were placed with search.py on the default render and fixed by hand on the matching plate (a mint mass, the bark, the disc, the ground, the whole plate).

limits: Benchmark 88.7 % mean. The bark patch scores lowest (histogram 51 %, autocorrelation 63 %): the reference trunk at that spot is 64 % key with the pink figure's arm crossing it, the rebuild's trunk is 43 % key with the mint streaking through; the bark lines are drawn as a broken scribble, not traced.

The hatched-mass patch misses on the ground ink color (47 %) because the reference patch contains pink where the rebuild has mint; whole-plate shares are matched by the count and size of the masses, not by position.
The reference's human figure is not redrawn; Mindgut's robot stands in its place, drawn with the same 4 px key.
The ground is the reference's own 235, 236, 222; alternates use cool or neutral grounds.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
